quest.title: Where the Roses Bloom
quest.description: Where shall the gun barrel of justice point? And who shall the bullet strike...?
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x20, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Goooood morning! Ayaka and I were just talking about you!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Is Chevreuse... still not joining us today?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Probably not, we haven't seen her, either.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Huh? But that's such a pity... Director Furina said that we've only got a few small scenes left before wrapping up the entire thing!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: She even said that she'll get me into a couple scenes so everyone will have a chance to shine in front of the Kamera!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: We were also planning on having a victory feast once we're all finished filming. You can join us, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Of course.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: If only Chevreuse was here... I still haven't taken a photo with her!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: I'm afraid that can't be helped. Those Special Patrol folks are like phantoms when they've got a case on their hands.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: But, to be honest, I am even more concerned by what I read in The Steambird earlier this morning. It said that... the killer in the murder case was none other than the author of "The Two Musketeers."

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah, I heard about that too! He came over and confessed his crimes, but gave no explanation as to why he pulled the trigger.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: We didn't know about this case at all when we joined the film. Is it going to affect the reception of our work...?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: From a pure publicity standpoint, this will draw a lot more attention to our film. I have to say, though, that no director can be perfectly comfortable with garnering attention through means other than artistic skill.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: To be fair, I feel like that ship sailed the moment you allowed yourself to be named as the director on our posters.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: It's not my fault that I'm super popular! What was that saying again? My popularity has—

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Sunk to an all-time low?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Spread to the four corners of Teyvat!

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Excuse me, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Xavier! Feels like it's been ages since we last saw you.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: I've been talking non-stop with the Film Association and I'm absolutely swamped trying to coordinate the film's marketing, so forgive me for not being around more often... But please believe me when I say that I will make sure everyone's hard work gets the exposure it deserves!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Seems like you've been fighting your own battles!

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Haha. Yes, that's one way to put it.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Oh, and before we begin the final round of filming, please allow me to finally introduce you to...

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: The original investor of our film, Mr. Morris.

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: ...A pleasure to meet you all.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Yes. Glad to make your acquaintance, Mr. Morris. We've heard about the issues you've encountered with your financial situation, and genuinely hope that things have taken a turn for the better.

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: Ah, well... the situation has indeed improved somewhat.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Mr. Morris! Accidents and last-minute challenges happen all the time. There's no need to blame yourself over it.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: The good news is that we're almost done filming now, and I would even say that this is the best story I've ever seen!

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: Is that so... I see, that's great news.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Alright, now that we've gotten all the pleasantries out of the way, let's get this show on the road.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: We'll mostly be filming typical people and scenery from the streets today to improve the sense of environmental ambiance in some parts of the film.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Oh, and there'll be a cameo for Mr. Kamisato and Miss Yoimiya as well. They'll be used to show outsider perspectives on the fates of the Two Musketeers.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: That's right. Ayato should be here any minute.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Excellent, then let's start with the scenery shots. Kamera and clapper loader, you're up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, we'll be ready!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Remember, all we need are some wide zoom shots of the streets. If you happen to find some particularly lovely patches of flowers and grass, feel free to grab some close-ups of those as well.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Ready? Lights, Kamera, ACTION!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Okay, now move the Kamera slowly.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Try to focus on that flower...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Take a close-up shot of the flower.)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hmm? What's wrong? Just adjust the focal length a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Take a close-up shot of the flower.)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Something the matter?

choices.text: The Kamera seems to be broken...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Huh!? But wasn't it working fine for all the days before?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Veronique! Can we try a different Kamera?

response.speaker: Veronique
response.text: No problem. How about this one?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Alright, let's give it another try. Lights, Kamera, action!
*mechanical malfunctioning noises*

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Don't tell me... This one is broken too!?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Veronique, do we have any other spare ones we can use?

response.speaker: Veronique
response.text: Uh... I'm afraid we only brought these two today.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: What!? Then go find a workshop to get them repaired right away! Oh, and you too, Bonnot. Go find our spare Kamera in the warehouse, and bring it back to the set!

response.speaker: Veronique
response.text: On it!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Greetings, everyone. My apologies for the delay. Hmm? Is something the matter, Ayaka?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: It seems like there are some issues with the filming equipment today. We're stuck for the moment...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I see...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Well, let's not just stand here twiddling our thumbs. Actors, to the makeup booth. We'll start on the next scene as soon as we get a working Kamera.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After some time, Veronique returns with a repaired Kamera...

response.speaker: Veronique
response.text: The people at the workshop told me that the part which holds the lens in place seemed to have fallen off. That's super strange... It was perfectly fine just yesterday.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Well, no time to dwell on that now. Let's get back to filming.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Quiet on set! Places, everyone! Lights, Kamera, action!

response.speaker: Person Chatting in the Street
response.text: By the way, have you heard about that recent murder case?

response.speaker: Person Chatting in the Street
response.text: Yes, I have. It seems that they've caused quite the commotion in the city.

response.speaker: Person Chatting in the Street
response.text: I heard that the chief of the Gardes is so mad about not catching the culprit that he's about to explode!

response.speaker: Person Chatting in the Street
response.text: Oh? I find that quite hard to imagine, considering how he already looks most days...

response.speaker: Bonnot
response.text: Director! Director!! We have a problem!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: We're in the middle of a take! Couldn't you wait until we wrapped up this scene!?

response.speaker: Bonnot
response.text: No, Director, our film — all the finalized film that we've been keeping in the case has disappeared!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Wait, what did you say!?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: ...Mr. Bonnot, please take me to where the film was kept right away!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I'm coming, too!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: No, Yoimiya! You have to stay here.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Okay, listen up. Everyone who's not working on this current scene can go with Bonnot to look for the film. Everyone else, stay put and wrap up the scene.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Unbelievable... How could all these problems happen in just one day?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After some time...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: We're back.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: How did it go? Did you find the film?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: We found it in the sewers.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Huh! In the sewers!? Is the film still okay?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: We discovered it just in time, so we should still be able to salvage it. The others are checking now to see if we lost any specific scenes.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Whew... You scared me for a moment there. I nearly thought we had lost everything...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I really don't want to experience that feeling of despair again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, but who could have stolen the film and dumped it there?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Could it be... some competitors working on other films?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But if they wanted to harass us, why wait until the last day?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Okay, we don't have time to really look into it right now. Let's strike while the iron is still hot, and wrap this thing up once and for all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Let's finish it!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Thanks to everyone's efforts, you finally wrap up the final scenes of the film...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Even though unexpected situations and problems struck during the filming process, you were able to overcome them all...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I would like to officially announce that our entry to the Festival, "The Two Musketeers," has now concluded filming!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh... Paimon is spent. It's so late already...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Even though the filming process proved to be extremely challenging, everyone provided valuable and unique contributions to the final product. Thank you all for your dedication and support!

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: And just like Director Furina, I would also like to extend my most heartfelt thanks to all of you. Really... you've all helped me so much. I just...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Alright, alright, let's save the awards speech for later, and hopefully also get some rehearsals in before the real thing.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Anyway, now it's time to party! Let's all make our way to the beach and have a celebration feast so loud and fun that even the Blubberbeasts will want in!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Ayato! How's your work been going?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Everything went rather smoothly. Thank you for your concern.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Ayato told me that we've already confirmed the dates for some Inazuma-Fontaine cultural exchange events.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: So the next time we visit, we'll be doing so in our capacities as the representatives of the Yashiro Commission.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohh, that's great! Then maybe Paimon will be able to find Fontaine detective novels in Inazuma from now on!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh wait... Wouldn't Yae Miko get upset if that happens? That would be stealing some of her business.

choices.text: As long as the novels are sufficiently interesting...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You've got a point... She's always complaining that light novels have become bland and too predictable, after all.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: The cultural exchange won't only feature literatures of both nations, of course. We have also made plans for cross-cultural engagements in the fields of gourmet cuisine, toymaking, and artisan craftsmanship.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, Paimon's getting super excited now!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: When the time comes, be sure to visit and participate in all the events.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Furina!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Oh, my darling clapper loader and Kamera operator! You've both worked really hard.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thinks you worked even harder than us! Honestly, Paimon was getting a little tired of playing with the clapperboard by the end of it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Worst of all, Paimon's started having dreams of you shouting "Lights, Kamera, ACTION!" into Paimon's ears! The actual dream can't even start until you've yelled that!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hey, if anything, shouldn't I be more grand and delightful in your dreams!? We've been through so much together and that's how your brain remembers me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, that's... That's not Paimon's fault! We've just used the clapperboard too much lately...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Anyway, what's most important is that we've wrapped the film. I'm pretty confident that we'll take first prize!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You mean, the Furina Award?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hey, no need to mention the official name!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, now that you mention it, if we did win the Prize, would Furina just get... a statue of herself?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Come on, I don't need that kind of attention. Xavier can accept the reward on our behalf.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But just imagine... Furina accepting the Furina Award, and holding a Furina statue...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: ...I'm going back to my dessert now. You all can keep discussing that on your own.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: This is turning out to be quite the party...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chiori!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Hey, you two.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you not really into these kinds of big social occasions?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Not particularly, but this is still better than Fontaine Fashion Week.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, but if this film becomes a big hit, people will definitely come flocking to your shop!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Yes, that's highly likely... as long as the film can premiere as planned.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you still worried about the case?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: That, and all the obstacles we had to face today.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, you're right... It's as if all our bad luck just manifested at once.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: But why today, of all days...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: No... No, it's nothing. We've already delivered the film to the editors, so there should be nothing more to worry about.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: How are you doing, Mr. Morris? You having a good time?

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: Well... You could say that. Do you happen to know when the party is scheduled to end?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Haha, judging by how much fun everyone's having, I'd say probably not until well after midnight.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Is there something that you still have to take care of at home, Mr. Morris?

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: Ah... I uh, I'm just not a late night person, so I might take off shortly.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh no! Silly me, I almost forgot something super important!

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: Oh... Uh, what is it?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I prepared a whole batch of fireworks for the party, but I forgot to bring them over from the warehouse!

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: Fireworks, you say? That's, uh, truly a pity. Sorry things didn't go as planned...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Could you help me carry them over, Mr. Morris? I won't be able to fetch all of them by myself...

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: Me? Uh... Are you sure that you can't find anyone else?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Haha, I just wanted to make this a surprise for everyone! The warehouse isn't far from here. We'll be there in no time.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Pretty please, Mr. Morris! These are some of the best fireworks I've ever made, so I also want you to see them before you leave. They're stunning — I promise that they'll be an once-in-a-lifetime experience that you'll never forget!

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: It's okay, just come with me! If we're sneaky enough, nobody else will see us leaving...

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: *sigh* Oh, alright...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Have you ever seen a fireworks show, Mr. Morris? It's pretty amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: Hmm, I'm afraid I haven't... But I'll take your word for it.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Wait, what's going on? This wasn't in the script!

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Drop the gun, Veronique!

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: ...Why? Why would you keep me from exacting revenge on this heartless monster?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Drop your weapon! This is my final warning.

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: What... What is going on...?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Do I have to spell it out for you, Morris? Everything that took place just now was staged to get you to confess the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: But this last part is all improv, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Chevreuse, you told us that you wanted us to help you stage a play, you never said anything about the "Second Musketeer"!

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: It's because even I had no way to confirm my theory until now.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Thank you for your performance, Yoimiya. Could I trouble you to go and bring in the other Special Patrol members? They should be on standby just outside.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Oh, and please tell the other cast members not to worry about us. We'll be rejoining them shortly.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: On it!

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: So, what do you think, Morris? Care to talk about what happened twenty years ago?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: My patience is limited, you know. Don't force me to take you back to the interrogation room... I'd wager that you wouldn't last for more than a minute in there.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: With the recording we made, you have no chance of winning in court. Cooperating with us now is the most practical move.

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: ...Alright, I'll talk.

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: I hired an assassin to murder Elisa.

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: She once worked as a maid on my family's estate. She was very beautiful, and after some time I fell for her.

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: We kept our relationship a secret, and carried out an affair for some time. But it wasn't long before she became pregnant.

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: If my parents ever found out, they would have stripped me of my inheritance and status, and driven me out of my home...

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: I also didn't expect Elisa to insist on bringing the pregnancy to term. She even asked me to leave my family, and travel far, far away with her.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: She believed that you were truly in love with her.

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: ...I didn't have a choice.

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: I gave her a large sum of Mora, told her to leave the family, and get rid of the baby.

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: But then years later, she sent me a letter. There were photos of two children, and she even asked if I could find some time to visit them...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Two children? Paimon thought Baptiste was the only... Ah! You mean...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Even if she had the children against your will, you could have just ignored her letter entirely. Why kill her?

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: I had just gotten engaged to be married to an heiress from another wealthy family, so if anyone were to find out about Elisa, my life would be completely ruined! I didn't have a choice!

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: No... you always had a choice. You just made the wrong choice, again.

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: ...Do you know how it feels to watch your mother be killed right in front of you?

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: My brother and I were hardly even school-age yet! We were hidden beneath the floorboards, grasping each other's hands like a lifeline. We were so terrified that we didn't even know when we could ever take a breath!

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: All we could do was to watch mother try to fight back, and then... collapse to the floor...

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: Even after the assassin left, we were still too terrified to leave our hiding spot. We thought that he might come back... It was only until the next evening when we finally climbed out and gathered around our mother.

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: But she... had already become cold and stiff to the touch.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: You made up your mind right then and there to bring this case to light.

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: Not only that... we resolved to get our revenge.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: And that's why you became the musketeers.

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: No, that's why I became a musketeer. The man from before was also killed by me. My brother had nothing to do with it.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I figured as much.

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: ...You did?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I once told these two that he didn't look like a killer to me. His confession from that night also rubbed me the wrong way.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I think what really tipped me off was... how could I not feel a sense of "regret" in him?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: He confessed faster than any criminal I've ever met, but he didn't say a single word about you. He insisted that he was the sole perpetrator in the case...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: But after the questioning ended, I disassembled the musket we dug up from his backyard, put it in front of him, and told him to reassemble it. Wanna guess how far he got?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: He had no idea where to even start. He's never touched a gun in his life.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Based on that, I determined that he was not acting alone. He only surrendered himself to draw our attention and create a moment of opportunity for his partner. So, I decided to play along.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: And as expected, the second musketeer followed us without hesitation once she saw Morris get separated from the rest of the cast.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Besides, why else would he call the novel "The TWO Musketeers"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... How did you know it was Veronique?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I figured it out the moment Baptiste told me his father's name.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: That so-called "financial crisis" was all just a ruse. He just wanted to sign up as the investor, and then leave the film without any source of funding.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: After all, he has a vested interest in minimizing the reach of this story. It's really just the same thing as what he did to Elisa all those years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: ...Human scum.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: But then Xavier pulled out all the stops and got the film made, against all odds. Morris couldn't have that.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: With the killer in custody, he figured it was safe to act. And so he came to visit the set today, just as I expected.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... so you were behind all those mishaps today!?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: As for the identity of the second musketeer... I assumed they'd probably stay close to Morris, and look for an opening.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: And if they already knew that Morris was the film's investor, then that narrowed the list of potential suspects as well.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Furthermore, being the props manager would allow the culprit to avoid scrutiny by purchasing mechanical parts in the name of the crew.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: With that hypothesis in mind, I went back to check Baptiste's orphanage adoption records. Guess whose name I saw on the same page, just a few lines from his?

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: My brother... He trusted you...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: As in, he trusted me to perform the deed on his behalf?

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: He trusted you to stand on the side of justice!

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I am.

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: I thought you could do it as well! The look on your face when you told him to go to hell... I really thought you'd put a bullet in his brain!

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: You know what he has done. Are you telling me that you'd rather see him spend the rest of his life living like a king in the Fortress of Meropide!?

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: I will never be able to forget the feeling of my mother's cold, lifeless hands... And you would call this ending fair? Is this what you call justice!?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I won't lie, Veronique. I did hesitate when your brother first told me about the truth...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I wondered... I agonized over whether I should really put a bullet in his head.

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: So why don't you...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Because that should never be how justice is carried out in this world!

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Perhaps, to you justice is simply reciprocated: an eye for an eye, and a life for a life.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: But everyone has their own understanding of justice. If everyone were to pursue their own definition of it, there would be no more order in this world.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Today, you'll kill Morris. And tomorrow? His children may come for you.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: The world cannot render judgments based on a desire for revenge. That will only lead to a cycle of revenge, as well as the destruction of order and civilized society.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Fontaine is founded on a set of laws and a standardized code of justice. That is why we are the Nation of Justice.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: But with all that said, I will promise you this: Morris will not lead a cushy life in the Fortress of Meropide.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Chevreuse, the rest of the Special Patrol is here.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Thank you so much, Yoimiya. Letellier, Turenna, please take them away.

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: ...I still can't agree with your reasoning.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: ...I know.

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: Justice has not been delivered. At least... not today.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chevreuse...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Let's go. We should give an explanation to the crew.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Thank you for your concern. I'm fine.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I'm just thinking... About the things in life that have driven people to take justice into their own hands.

choices.text: I think you made the right call.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Who would have thought Morris would turn out to be... Ugh, I'm at a loss for words. How could he have done something like this!?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I'm just glad that you are all safe and sound. Who knew that such a labyrinth of cases would be behind this story...

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Well... what should we do now? We have a finished film, of course, but... Should we still go ahead with the premiere?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: What do you mean!? Shouldn't you be even more motivated to spread the word now that you've learned the truth?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Chiori is right. I'd also like more people to see this story for themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: But the real ending of the story seems to have deviated somewhat from the one in the script. Is that still acceptable to you, Miss Chevreuse?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: The call is yours. We still have time to re-shoot an ending if that's what you'd like.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: ...No, it's fine as-is. I like what we have for the catharsis.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Romanticism is what gives works of art their appeal. Fiction is able to explore means of restitution that could never work in real life.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Just like the real world, the world of stories also has its own set of "rules" and "justice." These different possibilities are what initially drew me to reading in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Sounds good to me! I support your decision.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: What about Veronique... will she be okay?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: She will soon face her judgment alongside her brother and Morris.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: If I had to guess, they'll probably all be sent to the Fortress of Meropide. I'll make sure to give Wriothesley a heads-up about it.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Oh, you mean, "that" kind of heads-up?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Exactly.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Ahem, alright! Then the matter's settled! Now that everything's been taken care of, there's no reason for us to keep looking all gloomy and grumpy.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Let's get back to the feast and enjoy each other's company. We'll be starting the post-production process tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: You should join us, Chevreuse. You missed the first few hours of the party, didn't you?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Alright, count me in.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Then I'll wait for you over there. There's still some good news that I'd like share with Chevreuse.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon? Could you wait for me by the sea after the party ends? I'd like to go on a brief walk with the two of you.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Thank you very much.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Sorry for the wait.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, we weren't waiting long at all! Is there something else you wanted to tell us?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: No, I don't have anything new to share. I just felt that... since you were my investigation partners, I should have another conversation with the two of you.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: #{NICKNAME}... how would you have responded to Baptiste's request if you were in my shoes?

choices.text: I would have done the same as you.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Is that so... Thanks for sharing.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: ...When I was young, my father often took me here to swim. We'd come, rain or shine, even when it was freezing cold.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: He told me that swimming was the best activity to train one's strength of will. You could never give up before reaching the shore... especially when the water was cold.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? Why's that?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Because the moment you give up would be the moment you die. At that point, I still hadn't received my Vision.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: One winter, the chilly wind felt almost like knives on my skin, and the seawater was so frigid that it numbed my toes the moment I stepped in.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I cried and begged my father to spare me from having to swim across, but he wouldn't listen. He used to be a member of the Special Patrol as well... You could say it was his way of educating his children.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That sounds awful...

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: When he saw that I wouldn't stop crying, he just picked me up, and tossed me into the icy water.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: The bone-chilling cold took away my senses. I couldn't feel anything but fear and rage...

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I waited for my father to save me, but one look and I knew he'd already started swimming for the opposite shore. I realized that if I were to give up, I really would die right then and there.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I used all of my strength to try and catch up to my father. Those few minutes felt longer than my whole life up until that point. I did, however, make it to the other side.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I've never felt afraid about anything in my life after that, nor have I ever cried again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That way of teaching would have never worked on Paimon...

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Yeah, I don't think that was the right method for anyone...

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: It's just that... working now as I am in the pursuit of justice, I still sometimes feel like I've been tossed into that winter sea all over again. The anger and the helplessness...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Chevreuse...

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: But the worse I feel, the more I know to never give up. The alternative would be to forever lose myself among the waves.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Anyway, how about a race? Neither of us will drown, but we can still see who swims faster?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm game.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Er... You guys go ahead! Paimon will grab the clapperboard to mark the start of the race...

choices.text: I would have helped him get his revenge.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Hah... Just like the protagonist of the story, huh. Can't say it doesn't suit you.

talks.objective: Have a swimming contest with Chevreuse
Have a swimming contest with Chevreuse
Have a swimming contest with Chevreuse

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Whoa, that felt good!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You were so fast in the water, Chevreuse... You were swimming even faster than Paimon could fly!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, about the Special Patrol... Did you join because of your dad?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Partly, but I'd say I was more inspired the heroes I read about in stories growing up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so it's due to your love of stories...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Of course, it was only after I joined the Special Patrol that I learned that truth is often stranger than fiction.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: ...Come on, let's walk a bit more.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Thank you for coming on this walk with me. I feel a lot better after getting all that off my chest.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!? We're nearly back at Baptiste's house!

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Huh, you're right. I didn't realize we were so close.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He really did plant a lot of flowers. It's just like how he described it in the story.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: #*gasp* Wait. Paimon, {NICKNAME}, look!

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: The Rainbow Roses in the garden... They're in full bloom now.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: I was thinking... If this film turns out to be a success, could I ask the two of you to stay and be a part of my crew?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Of course, I'll definitely... increase the pay for next time!

dialogues.speaker: Bonnot
dialogues.text: I'd be more than happy to, Mr. Xavier.

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: Thank you for the offer, Mr. Xavier, but I've made some plans to go on a journey to the other nations once the festival is over...

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Is that so... Well then, in that case, bon voyage, Miss Veronique. Please feel free to get in touch once you've returned to Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Ah... I wish we could have spent some more time here.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Don't worry, it won't be long before we're back again.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hmm... What kind of dessert should I try next?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, we haven't seen Chevreuse since that night at Baptiste's place...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, guess there's no point worrying about it now! Let's go join up with the others.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Party! Party! Paimon wants to party!!!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! This place is hopping! Everyone's finally getting to relax after wrapping up the film.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go chat with someone!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: The warehouse is right over here... I moved the fireworks there in advance, so it shouldn't be too much work bringing them back.

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: ...It's still a ways away from the party.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Hahaha, sorry 'bout that, Mr. Morris! It's probably because I'm used to carrying fireworks all the time, so it doesn't feel like a lot of work to me.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: To be honest, I do sometimes question whether the decisions I make are the right ones.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: But I know that no matter what, I must keep swimming.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Because the only thing I've got my eyes on is the shore in the distance.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You explain everything that happened to the rest of the crew...
